subject.title: RFC 0010: ACL-based memory partitioning and cross-user access

question: Should OpenClaw accept session-scoped ACL memory isolation as RFC 0010’s normative core, including core-owned identity validation and fail-closed group-membership semantics?
rationale: This is a product and security-boundary choice with durable storage, identity, and upgrade implications; documentation review alone cannot establish that the proposed core boundary matches maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped normative core
options.body: Accept only the explicitly bounded isolation core after a maintainer threat-model review and a linked discussion records the supported deployment assumptions.

options.title: Keep it exploratory
options.body: Retain the proposal as non-normative design material until maintainers choose the memory-security roadmap and implementation owner.

options.title: Request a narrower RFC
options.body: Ask for a smaller proposal focused on one enforceable boundary before committing to broker, identity, schema, and operational contracts together.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped normative core
recommendation.body: Accept only the explicitly bounded isolation core after a maintainer threat-model review and a linked discussion records the supported deployment assumptions.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal author is the only concrete document owner visible in the available branch history; a repository maintainer must still make the acceptance decision.
